To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the current protein intake of the general population in developed countries is adequate for most healthy people; b) protein requirements are higher during pregnancy and lactation, c) protein intake should be higher in the elderly to maintain lean body mass, d) the protein requirements of athletes are higher than those of the general population, and e) the protein requirements for the critically ill are higher than those for the general population.
the average protein requirement of healthy adults is 0.83 g protein/kg body weight (0.36 g nitrogen/kg body weight) per day.
The protein requirements for healthy adults are 0.66 g/kg/day for adults with adequate energy intake, 0.8 g/kg/day for pregnant and lactating women, and 1.2 g/kg/day for children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of proteins.
the development and use of new technologies to improve the quality of life for people living with chronic diseases.
the study of the effects of protein intake on body composition and health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein requirements for adults are between 0.66 g/kg and 0.83 g/kg of body weight.
a daily intake of 0.8 g protein/kg body weight is sufficient to maintain nitrogen balance in most healthy adults.
, based on the available evidence, a protein intake of approximately 1 g/kg/d in healthy adults is sufficient to maintain positive nitrogen balance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein requirement for healthy adults is 0.66 g/kg body weight (BW) per day.
we have shown that the current protein recommendations for healthy adults are too high.
the protein requirements for healthy adults were estimated to be 0.66 g protein per kg body weight (BW) per day, with a 95% confidence interval (95% CI) from 0.55 to 0.77 g per kg per day.

we need to do more research on the protein requirements of vegans, vegetarians, and other groups of people who don't eat animal products.
